top_signals.title: Nodal Exchange Planning AI Compute Futures to Rival CME, ICE
top_signals.summary: Nodal Exchange Holdings, LLC is seeking to launch futures contracts on computing power for artificial intelligence chips, joining a host of firms rushing to do the same.
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that with Hugging Face, the chipmaker will "expand access to AI for developers and institutions worldwide."

top_signals.title: Japan expected to forgo second extra budget for fiscal 2026
top_signals.summary: The remaining amount of general reserve funds is around ¥800 billion. In addition, about ¥1.9 trillion is left in reserve funds for responses to the situation in the Middle East.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Great British Summer Savings: millions of pounds saved by families
top_signals.summary: Hard working families across the UK have saved millions of pounds over the summer thanks to the Government’s Great British Summer Savings.

top_signals.title: Rising Yields Seen Pushing Companies to Sell Bonds Sooner
top_signals.summary: Wall Street dealers were already bracing for a potential record in September for high-grade US corporate bond sales, and recent surging yields may give the blue-chip companies even more reason to borrow now before funding costs rise further.

top_signals.title: Are financial rules fuelling the Premier League’s record transfer spending?
top_signals.summary: Premier League football’s financial regulations may have been designed to control transfer spending but they actually incentivise it, argues Danny Hill. Premier League clubs spent a record £3.46bn this summer. top_signals.title: Why Uranium Stocks Are Falling as U.S. Production Triples
top_signals.summary: U.S. uranium production is climbing from a base so depleted that a threefold increase still leaves America dependent on imports for most of its reactor fuel. Output rose to 2.1 million pounds in 2025, its highest level since 2017, before reaching 2.13 million pounds in the first half of 2026, according to the EIA. Second-quarter production increased 4.7% to 1.09 million pounds. U.S. nuclear-plant operators purchased 46.9 million pounds of uranium in 2025, more than 22 times the amount produced domestically.
